title: Template
description: A vehicle trim-configuration template: one model-year, plus the trims it shipped in. This is the object Console edits and R2 serves. Attributes true of every trim live on `attributes`; anything that differs between trims lives on that trim. A VIN decode narrows this template to exactly one trim and emits a Resolved document.

id.description: manufacturer-slug _ model-slug _ year. The only identifier. There is no ksuid, no legacy id, and no on-chain table backing this.

deviceType.description: DeviceType id whose vocabulary this template is validated against.

manufacturer.title: TemplateManufacturer
manufacturer.description: Denormalised into the template on purpose. Reading a template must not require a second lookup, and creating one must not require the brand to have on-chain storage provisioned first.

tokenId.description: Manufacturer NFT, when one exists. Optional: it grants direct-edit rights, it is not a precondition for the template to exist.

hardwareTemplateId.description: Which DIMO hardware configuration this vehicle takes. NOT a vehicle attribute: it describes what our gear does with the car, not what the car is, so it sits outside `attributes` and is never validated against the DeviceType vocabulary. Template-level value is the default for every trim; a trim may override it. Today `common/utils.go:202` stamps "130" on every definition and exactly 3 style rows override it. Contribution-gated: an open contributor must not be able to change what hardware we ship.

trims.description: At least one. A model-year sold in a single configuration has exactly one trim; that is still a trim, not a special case.

version.description: Increments on every published edit. Immutable once written: t/<id>/v/<version>.json is the permanent record.

author.description: Address that published this version. Every edit is attributed.

name.description: As the manufacturer markets it: "XSE V6", "Hybrid LE", "Long Range AWD".

selectors.description: How a decoded VIN is matched to this trim. Omit on a single-trim template.

hardwareTemplateId.description: Overrides the template's value for this trim only. Omit unless this trim genuinely takes different hardware.

selectors.title: TrimSelectors
selectors.description: Signals from the VIN decoder. A trim matches when every selector present matches. Most specific match wins; ties are a template defect and must be reported, not silently broken.

manufacturerCode.description: OEM model/option code. Already present in today's data as manufacturer_code, where it sits on the model-year record doing nothing — it is a trim key that was flattened.

styleName.description: Style string as the upstream decoder reports it. Matched case-insensitively.

vinPattern.description: Anchored regex over the 17-character VIN for OEMs that encode trim positionally.

attributeMap.title: AttributeMap
attributeMap.description: name -> value. On the template these are the attributes shared by every trim; on a trim they are that trim's own. An attribute is either on the template or on a trim, never both. Names must exist in the DeviceType; enum values must appear in that attribute's options. An attribute that is unknown is ABSENT — never "" and never "<nil>". 6% of today's attribute rows are one of those two placeholders; this schema makes them unrepresentable.

additionalProperties.description: Typed, not stringified. fuel_tank_capacity_gal is 15.8, not "15.800000".
